source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling publishes 24 MW of IT capacity in 154,230 square feet, placing it 17th among Virginia's 25 data centers with disclosed power figures and representing 1.5% of the state's announced capacity.

At the common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this capacity suggests roughly 600 racks. The facility's rank within Virginia reflects adequate scale for regional compute demand, but leaves unresolved whether it can serve the high-density GPU workloads that define AI infrastructure. CyrusOne has published no certifications for this campus and discloses neither its acceptance density nor any upgradeable power headroom beyond the stated 24 MW. These gaps matter because a facility without room to scale becomes a dead end as AI workloads grow.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities but only 25 publish power figures. Sterling's data comes from operator specifications, not independent measurement. Whether this campus becomes material to AI scaling depends on what CyrusOne does not disclose: whether it accepts the high-density cooling and power distribution that AI training requires, whether additional power can reach it from Northern Virginia's grid, and whether the operator plans announced expansion. The state's transparency gap makes it impossible to know whether Sterling represents available capacity or merely historical infrastructure.
